# Gradient-source closure and compatible label bodies in integer rank one

This uses the ACTUAL deepest-source and full-space transport hypotheses of `candidate 3b257d8ddacb6167`. It is not a statement about arbitrary concave piecewise-affine parameters or detached moment data. It proves a bounded compatibility result, not a classwise Gamma payment.

## 1. The enlarged source class is a closed minor

For a continuous gradient c define J_c to consist of every proper deepest base p whose unique proper deepest mark Y_p has ALL active finite planes of L sharing continuous gradient c. This includes the positively weighted source set J_c^+; it may also include sigma-zero sources.

Suppose p_j belong to J_c, lambda_j>0, sum lambda=1, and r=sum lambda_j p_j is an integer. Compatibility and completeness put the averaged mark Y=sum lambda_j Y_(p_j) in the r-fiber. Buffered deepest superlevels are convex. The strict atomic-depth superlevel {b_base>Q} is also convex. Thus Y is a proper deepest mark, and uniqueness identifies it as Y_r.

At an attained own-proper cap there, the exact upper Q-quantile and concavity of f force

    f(Y_r)=sum_j lambda_j f(Y_(p_j)).

Writing f=M^(-1/N)L^(1/N)(E^(1/d))^(d/N), positivity and strict monotonicity of the weighted geometric mean force

    L(Y_r)=sum_j lambda_j L(Y_(p_j)).                    (1)

Every finite affine plane A active at Y_r majorizes L. Its averaged nonnegative gaps at the inputs have sum zero by (1); therefore it touches every input. Its continuous gradient must equal c. This applies to EVERY active plane at Y_r, so r belongs to J_c.

Consequently

    J_c=P intersect conv(J_c).                         (2)

The equality is understood for nonempty J_c and the original complete base. Distinct classes J_c and J_b have disjoint occupied base parities. Indeed equal-parity marks from the two classes have an integer proper deepest midpoint; the same active-plane argument forces c=b. Neither step requires positive sigma at the intervening mark.

This strengthens the positive-source parity statement but says nothing by itself about the bases occupied by the TARGET region of a label.

## 2. One positive source gives a convex target representative

Let c be an occurring target label with exactly one positive source Y_i. Choose any active plane A_i at that source and put

    D_i=C intersect {A_i=L}
       =C intersect intersection_r {A_i<=A_r}.           (3)

D_i is compact convex. Let R_c denote the almost-everywhere target region {grad_X L=c}. Since every row preserves its label and this is the only positive row of label c,

    q_i=1 on R_c and q_i=0 outside R_c, nu-a.e.          (4)

The actual contact identity gives R_c subset D_i modulo mixed-null sets. Conversely, away from the finite union of continuous-gradient tie hyperplanes in a fiber, any point of D_i has active continuous gradient c. Hence

    dm restricted to R_c =dm restricted to D_i.         (5)

This is an equality of measures in EVERY sampled fiber, since there are finitely many fibers. It is not a claim about individual boundary points where the gradient is undefined.

The actual fibers (D_i)_z=D_i intersect ({z} times R^d) form a compatible convex family: every anchored combination is contained in the corresponding target section. Empty and lower-dimensional fibers are retained. Equivalently take the canonical hull of all its sampled sections; this reproduces those same sections at every integer base because D_i is convex. Its full sampled projection is lattice-complete in that canonical projection. The set of bases having positive d-volume is also a closed minor: positive input sections contain small balls, so every positive anchored combination has positive volume.

Thus a one-source label really does possess a physical convex mixed representative. This conclusion uses the full source/target allocation, rather than treating arbitrary unions of contact cells as convex.

## 3. All labels admit convex representatives in integer rank at most one

Assume the inherited integer affine lattice of P has rank one. If only one target label occurs, it occupies all original mixed volume by the label identity, so the original canonical C itself is a compatible convex representative.

Suppose at least two labels occur. If one label c had two distinct positive sources p<q, Section 1 would fill every integer base between them with proper deepest marks of the same unique continuous gradient c. This interval includes both inherited lattice parities. Every positive source of another label shares a parity with one of these marks, contradicting the disjoint-parity conclusion of Section 1. Therefore every occurring label has exactly one positive source. There are at most two labels, and Section 2 supplies a compatible convex representative for each.

Rank zero is immediate: there is one possible proper deepest base and hence one positive source/label.

No disjointness of the closed representative boundaries is claimed; they can meet in lower-dimensional sections. Their d-dimensional mixed measures partition the original mixed measure because their labels do so.

## 4. The exact obstruction to the same argument in higher rank

For any occurring gradient c define on real bases of C

    F_c(z)=max_(X in C_z) [L(z,X)-c.X].                 (6)

The actual maximizers exist. Combining maximizing points proves that F_c is concave. The closed c-maximizer region in each fiber is

    B_z^c={X in C_z:L(z,X)-c.X=F_c(z)},                 (7)

a convex set. At fiber-interior differentiability points it agrees with the label region. The key anchored calculation is exact: if X_j belong to B_(z_j)^c and z=sum lambda_j z_j, then their average is a maximizer whenever

    F_c(z)=sum lambda_j F_c(z_j).                       (8)

Indeed concavity puts its value at least at the right side and the definition of F_c bounds it above by the left side. Without (8), the concavity argument allows a strict gap and does not prove membership in B_z^c.

Every individual transport row is confined to an affine contact face of F_c, because its source active plane has the form c.X+a.z+b and majorizes L on C. Different rows of the SAME continuous gradient can have different base contact planes. Rowwise contact equalities do not imply (8) between targets belonging to different rows. The rank-one parity argument removes exactly this multiple-source/multiple-label configuration; no analogous removal is proved here in higher rank.

In particular this note supplies no higher-rank incompatible-label example with actual deepest sources. Such an example would need to preserve their heredity and the full continuous martingale, rather than using arbitrary concave maximizer profiles.

## 5. Compatibility alone still does not pay the proposed class budget

The actual one-gradient calibration `candidate 7738d044742e9b61` already has a compatible full target family, zero covariance/entropy defect, a unique proper deepest source, strict closed-minor quotas, and a globally optimal parameter for its fixed body. Its class Gamma payment nevertheless fails. Therefore the positive compatibility theorem above is only a geometric structural gain. It cannot be turned into Gamma times class mass divided by SOURCE parity count without a new joint body-minimum argument or another actual cap estimate.
